contradiction_discovered: RFC §9.2/§9.3 give 'before DISPATCHED ⇒ UNRUNNABLE' for a harness that failed to operate, but the reference probe decided 'before DISPATCHED' from two independent channels racing in one queue: the anchor's exit notice (the _exited thread) and the target's protocol lines (the _pump thread, from the output pipe the anchor also held open). When the exit notice won, an already-written READY was never read and a target that had completed its protocol and exited 0 was recorded as 'did not start' — a false UNRUNNABLE on one party and a false VERIFIER_DISAGREEMENT between two. The defect is in harness observation ordering, not in product behaviour.

replacement.summary: Two independent facts, never collapsed. The anchor points its fd 2 at the null device right after spawning the target (range_anchor._release_output), so the output stream's end of file is the target's and its descendants' own. The probe reads its protocol through one pump, which publishes every line and then STREAM_CLOSED from the same thread (the pump-completion barrier); the process's exit is asked of the range only after STREAM_CLOSED. Before DISPATCHED: the stream closed without the expected line and the exit reported ⇒ the existing typed harness failure; the stream closed with the process still running at the watchdog ⇒ harness timeout; a protocol tag out of order ⇒ the harness broke its protocol. After DISPATCHED: the stream closed without RESULT ⇒ the exit's provenance (§9.3), or the window expiring if the process still runs at W. A protocol line must be terminated. No drain window remains (_DRAIN_S and _exited removed).
